content: Eating patterns refer to the overall selection of foods and beverages that an individual consumes on a regular basis. These patterns can include specific dietary approaches, such as the Mediterranean diet or the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet. However, no single dietary pattern is universally ideal for everyone. It is crucial to customize these dietary plans to meet the unique needs, preferences, and accessibility of each individual, particularly for effective diabetes management. Meal planning plays a critical role in managing diabetes, and the involvement of a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) is essential. An RDN can assist individuals with diabetes in creating a sustainable meal plan that aligns with their personal health goals and medical conditions. Evidence-based recommendations emphasize prioritizing non-starchy vegetables, whole grains, nuts, seeds, and low-fat dairy products. At the same time, it is important to minimize the consumption of processed foods and added sugars.
